body: Very cool! On my m2 MBA I setup a simple 30s benchmark scene moving a camera around bistro for various scaling factors and saw a roughly 19% improvement going from fsr2 to MetalFX temporal. MetalFX spatial also consistently was a few % faster than fsr1 and imo looks better.

Tested locally (rebased on top of `master`), it works as expected. ## Benchmark
Mac specifications - MacBook Pro 16 2024 - **SoC:** M4 Max 16-core CPU, 40-core GPU - **RAM:** 48 GB - **SSD:** 1 TB - **OS:** macOS 15.1.1
*Using https://github.com/godotengine/tps-demo with [MetalFX scaling options added](https://github.com/godotengine/tps-demo/pull/196). All tests done in fullscreen at native output resolution (3456x2234).* MetalFX performs slightly better than FSR1/2 in upscaling scenarios and generally looks a bit more stable. However, MetalFX temporal scaling lacks a sharpening option, goes for a softer look and has more noticeable stippling artifacts than FSR2, so it may not be to everyone's taste. This softer look has generally been noticed in tests in other games, so it's within expected bounds. The stippling artifacts are more questionable though. (This is another reason why games should expose both FSR2 and MetalFX temporal whenever possible.) ### FSR2 Quality ### MetalFX Temporal Quality ### Ultra Performance scaling factor Bilinear | FSR1 | MetalFX Spatial | FSR2 | MetalFX Temporal -|-|-|-|- 415 FPS (2.40 mspf) | 365 FPS (2.73 mspf) | 386 FPS (2.59 mspf) | 241 FPS (4.14 mspf) | 257 FPS (3.89 mspf) ### Native scaling factor Bilinear | FSR2 | MetalFX Temporal -|-|- 108 FPS (9.25 mspf) | 78 FPS (12.82 mspf) | 77 FPS (12.98 mspf)
Most of the PR looks pretty great to me. If my suggestions are addressed then I think this is good to go.
Left a request for one minor change, code LGTM otherwise.
